item.title: A Cut Finite Element Method with Boundary Value Correction for Robin, Neumann and Interface Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.17445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the cut finite element method with boundary value correction of Burman, Hansbo and Larson [Math.\ Comp.\ 87 (2018) 633--657] to Robin and Neumann conditions and to interface problems with imperfect bonding. The formulation retains a piecewise affine boundary for all integration, while using the exact geometry only at boundary quadrature points. The correction uses Taylor expansions of the solution and its gradient along the discrete normal, with the exact normal used to evaluate the transported flux. At an interface, a further correction to the normal flux jump accounts for the difference between these two normals. Under the stated trace and Poincar\'e bounds, the corrected form is an $O(h^{1/2})$ perturbation of a symmetric form, whose matrix can therefore be used as a preconditioner. For a fixed finite Robin coefficient, we obtain the energy error bound $C_\beta(h^p+\delta_h^{m+1})$, whereas the bound uniform in the Robin coefficient is $C(h^p+h^{-1/2}\delta_h^{m+1})$, provided the Poincar\'e constant is uniform. With $\delta_h=O(h^2)$, the sufficient Taylor orders are therefore $2m+2\ge p$ and $2m+\frac32\ge p$, respectively. Numerical examples for $p=1,2,3$ illustrate these rates and the effect of the flux-jump correction in the interface problem.
item.dc:creator: Erik Burman, Peter Hansbo, Mats G. Larson

item.title: Gusto: a toolkit for compatible finite element dynamical cores
item.description: arXiv:2611.17540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gusto is a tool for rapid prototyping of new algorithms based on compatible finite element methods for discretising the fluid equations in the dynamical core of weather and climate models. In this context, the development of new algorithms typically follows a path that involves testing on a hierarchy of simpler equation sets sharing important features of the mathematical structure of the equation set solved by the dynamical core. Gusto provides compatible finite element spatial discretisations of the hierarchy of equation sets, along with a range of timestepping schemes. The code is modular so that different spatial and temporal discretisations can be combined and the same schemes can be applied to any of the equation sets. This facilitates fair comparison of the schemes and makes the extension of any algorithmic developments to the more complex equation sets more straightforward. In this paper we present Gusto to the community by describing the algorithms implemented in Gusto and showcasing their performance through a variety of test problems commonly used in numerical weather prediction.
item.dc:creator: Jemma Shipton, Thomas M. Bendall, Colin J. Cotter, David M. Acreman, Timothy C. Andrews, Jack Betteridge, Alex Brown, Thomas H. Gibson, Nell Hartney, David A. Ham, Joshua Hope-Collins, Jeremy A. Pike, Connor J. Ward, Dan Witt

item.title: A Unified Framework for First- and Second-Order Energy-Stable Parametric Finite Element Methods for Planar Willmore Flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.17700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The construction of structure-preserving schemes for planar Willmore flow that are second-order accurate in time and avoid large coupled nonlinear solves remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified framework for first- and second-order fully discrete energy-stable parametric finite element schemes for planar Willmore flow with a length-penalization term. The framework is based on a new equivalent reformulation involving a global auxiliary variable. The main novelty lies in the second-order construction, which combines midpoint curvature quantities weighted by elementwise arc-length Jacobian ratios with a compatible discrete tangent to obtain exact discrete chain rules for the bending energy and curve length. A further contribution is to show that both schemes satisfy discrete modified energy dissipation laws that yield the same type of a priori bounds on the discrete solution as the original energy law. They also retain Barrett--Garcke--N{\"u}rnberg tangential motion to promote favorable mesh distribution. Each stage reduces to two linear solves with exactly the same coefficient matrix and one scalar nonlinear solve. We rigorously prove unique solvability of the linear subproblems under suitable assumptions and derive computable sufficient conditions for local existence and uniqueness of the scalar solution near unity. Numerical experiments demonstrate the expected temporal accuracy, energy dissipation, good mesh quality and computational efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoli Li, Yujing Yan

item.title: Convergence analysis of physics-informed neural networks for subdiffusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.17759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks have emerged as mesh-free solvers for partial differential equations, yet their rigorous convergence theory for time-fractional problems remains limited. We present a convergence analysis of PINNs for linear subdiffusion equations and for the associated backward problem of recovering the initial data from terminal observations. To address the nonlocality and weakly singular kernels of fractional derivatives, we introduce a discretization-based PINN framework built on some popular time-stepping schemes satisfying discrete maximal regularity, including backward Euler, BDF2, L1, and fractional CN schemes. This approach avoids the exact evaluation of fractional derivatives at training points while preserving the stability structure needed for convergence analysis. For the forward problem, we prove that, under the natural fractional maximal-regularity condition $u\in W^{\alpha,p}(0,T;L^2(\Omega))\cap L^p(0,T;H^2(\Omega)\cap H_0^1(\Omega))$, the piecewise linear temporal reconstructions of PINN-loss minimizers converge to the exact solution. This result avoids the higher-order regularity assumptions on the exact solution that are often imposed in existing PINN convergence analyses. We also verify the required discrete maximal regularity and consistency properties for the aforementioned popular time discretizations. We then extend the analysis to the backward subdiffusion problem and establish convergence of the regularized recovery of the initial data from terminal observations, despite its ill-posedness. Numerical experiments for both forward and backward problems support the theoretical results, demonstrate the necessity of regularization, and show that $L^2$-type losses alone are generally insufficient. These results establish a rigorous theoretical basis for discretization-based PINNs for time-fractional diffusion problems.
item.dc:creator: Bangti Jin, Qiqi Rao, Zhi Zhou

item.title: Compatible by Construction: Bottom-Up Nonlinear Model Reduction without Interface Bases
item.description: arXiv:2611.17773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear manifolds can provide compact representations of solutions to partial differential equations (PDEs), but generating training data and learning these representations on large domains remain costly. We present a bottom-up framework that reuses local nonlinear representations learned on a small training domain to solve larger PDE systems. A shared nonlinear decoder represents the full set of degrees of freedom owned by each subdomain, without separate interior and interface models. Each global degree of freedom has a unique owner, and local residuals directly use decoded state values from the corresponding neighboring subdomains. The resulting discrete state is single-valued by construction, eliminating the need for independent interface copies and additional interface compatibility constraints. Physical coupling is retained through the original time-discrete PDE residual. With the decoder held fixed, the subdomain-specific reduced coordinates are determined jointly by minimizing this residual, and the Gauss--Newton system is assembled from local contributions. Experiments on parameterized viscous Burgers and incompressible Navier--Stokes problems demonstrate reuse on larger domains without retraining. Comparisons with local proper orthogonal decomposition models under the same coupling construction show favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-offs in the tested regimes.
item.dc:creator: Youngkyu Kim, Youngsoo Choi

item.title: A narrow band method for non-causal discretizations of anisotropic eikonal equations, with adaptive width, sub-and super-solution construction, and quasi-linear complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.17947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a narrow band method for numerically solving anisotropic eikonal equations, and more generally static first order Hamilton-Jacobi equations with possibly non-convex Hamiltonians, discretized using standard schemes (semi-Lagrangian, upwind-differences, Lax-Friedrichs). The causality property is not needed, in contrast with the fast marching method. The proposed approach simultaneously builds a numerical sub-solution u and super-solution u to the problem, and adapts the width of the narrow band based on their comparison. We prove that (1 + $\epsilon$)u $\ge$ u at termination, where $\epsilon$ > 0 is any given tolerance parameter, and that the worst case complexity is O(N | ln $\epsilon$| ln(N/$\epsilon$)), where N denotes the number of discretization points, and the underlying constant is explicit in terms of those associated with the scheme properties. Numerical experiments illustrate our results.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Marie Mirebeau (CNRS, CB), Yanis Mouheb (CB, CEA/DAM)

item.title: A Realizability-Based Kinetic-Fluid Domain Decomposition Method for Single-Temperature Gas Mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2611.18068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a domain-adaptive numerical method for multi-species kinetic models that relax toward a single-temperature and single-velocity hydrodynamic limit. To this end, we derive moment realizability matrices for this regime. In this way the ideas of Levermore, Morokoff, and Nadiga are extended to non-equilibrium mixtures in which inter-species and intra-species collisions occur at comparable rates, so that all species relax to a common velocity and a common temperature. The realizability conditions are used as an indicator to divide the computational domain, at each time step, into macroscopic and kinetic regions. In the kinetic regions, where the continuum description fails (e.g., across strong shocks, non-equilibrium interfaces, or kinetic boundary layers), the method solves the multi-species kinetic equations. Close to local thermodynamic equilibrium, the Euler equations of the mixture are solved instead. Confining the kinetic computations to the non-equilibrium regions reduces the simulation time, while the results remain close to those of the full kinetic solver. The method is discretized on Cartesian grids with high-order schemes in space and time. The kinetic equations are integrated with an Asymptotic-Preserving Implicit-Explicit (IMEX) scheme, so that a consistent discretization of the single-velocity, single-temperature Euler system of the mixture is recovered when the Knudsen number goes to zero. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first realizability-based adaptive spatial domain decomposition method for gas mixtures in this single-velocity, single-temperature setting.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Caparello, Lorenzo Pareschi, Thomas Rey

item.title: High-order IMEX local discontinuous Galerkin methods with sparse grids for high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.18079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a high-order IMEX-LDG scheme on sparse grids for solving nonlinear parabolic PDEs in moderate to high dimensions. The method combines the advantages of LDG methods for convection--diffusion problems, IMEX-RK time integrators for stiff systems, and sparse-grid techniques to mitigate the curse of dimensionality. The resulting scheme is fully parallelized in MPI, is robust, efficient, and scalable, making it suitable for a wide range of applications involving high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Joel P. Villarino, Manuel J. Castro, J. A. Garc\'ia-Rodr\'iguez, J. G. L\'opez-Salas

item.title: Bound-preserving finite volume scheme for a coupled parabolic system with nonlinear and nonlocal drift
item.description: arXiv:2611.18090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a bound preserving finite-volume scheme for a coupled system of partial differential equations with nonlinear, nonlocal drift. The main contribution of this work is twofold: $(1)$ we show that the proposed scheme preserves physically motivated bounds; $(2)$ we prove that the scheme is well-posed and leads to a sequence of approximate solutions converging to the weak solution of the original problem. This setting is motivated by questions related to morphology formation in organic solar cells.
item.dc:creator: Nicklas J\"averg{\aa}rd, Adrian Muntean

item.title: An entropy-stable splitting strategy for a hyperbolic dispersive shallow-water model on unstructured meshes
item.description: arXiv:2611.18166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an entropy-stable splitting strategy for the numerical solution of a hyperbolic approximation of the Serre--Green--Naghdi (SGN) model, leading to an efficient solver for dispersive water waves on unstructured meshes. The model was introduced by Escalante et al. (2019) and justified shortly thereafter by Richard (2021) as an asymptotic model of the free-surface Euler equations under a weak compressibility assumption. While the parent model includes full topography terms and enhanced dispersive properties, the present study focuses on its mild-slope form without enhanced dispersion, which retains an exact energy equation, the cornerstone of the stability analysis. The splitting yields a shallow-water subsystem with two passive scalars, governed by the \textit{slow} gravity waves, and an acoustic subsystem carrying the dispersive effects, governed by the \textit{fast} acoustic waves. The gravity step adapts an existing entropy-stable scheme, while an original scheme is derived for the acoustic step; both dissipate the energy at the discrete level, under local fully discrete stability criteria on general unstructured meshes. Complementary linear analyses select the low-dissipation calibration of the gravity step used in the computations, outside the scope of the nonlinear estimate. The acoustic step, which requires no global linear solve, is sub-iterated after each gravity time step; the resulting solver is three to six times more expensive than a classical shallow-water solver, depending on the chosen acoustic speed. Numerical validations, ranging from academic benchmarks to a realistic coastal configuration, highlight the properties of the approach and pave the way for operational use.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Couderc, Arnaud Duran, Maria Kazakova, Bastien Lombard, Pascal Noble, R\'emy Baraille, Jean-Paul Vila

item.title: Kronecker Approximations of Covariance Matrices for Solving Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.18309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverse problems arise in many applications where the task is to recover unknown parameters from indirect or noisy observations. In contrast to forward problems, where outputs are directly computed from known inputs, inverse problems are designed to infer the underlying variables from the observed effect. Inverse problems are often ill-posed, so regularization is needed to compute reasonable solutions. One form of regularization incorporates prior knowledge about the unknown parameters in the form of prior distributions. However, in many settings, large prior covariance matrices pose computational bottlenecks for solving inverse problems. To address this, we study approximations of large covariance matrices via structured Kronecker-Toeplitz products and demonstrate how these approximations can be used to solve inverse problems. We exploit the Block-Toeplitz-Toeplitz-Block structure induced by the covariance kernel to construct compact approximations that are orders of magnitude cheaper to store and invert. These approximations are deployed as prior covariance surrogates in Bayesian inverse problems solved via generalized hybrid iterative methods. We demonstrate that the Kronecker-Toeplitz approximation attains lower relative approximation error than existing matrix approximations, exhibits rapid error decay with rank, and enables efficient matrix-vector products. Applications to 2D seismic tomography reconstruction problems illustrate the practical utility of these methods.
item.dc:creator: Srijon Sarkar, Julianne Chung

item.title: Score-based neural ordinary differential equations for reaction-diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A diffusion equation can be rewritten as a transport equation driven by the score function of the evolving density. Conventional probability-flow formulations, which move particles deterministically with this score-driven velocity, typically conserve total mass. In this work, we develop a Lagrangian method for reaction-diffusion equations in which each particle carries a position and a physical weight. The characteristic ODEs incorporate source terms into the evolution of the log-density and its gradient, while particle weights track changes in mass. We combine this representation with a learned velocity field and weighted particle training to approximate these dynamics. For non-increasing reaction rates, a relative-entropy inequality supports the mass-normalized self-consistency residual as the training objective. This objective can control the error of the induced density when the growth rate is bounded. The algorithm divides the time interval into short windows. In each window, a frozen velocity generates the particle data for a regression of the network velocity. We draw the particles from period-adapted initial sampling distributions and weight them in the loss partly by their predicted future mass, because the reaction can make regions with little initial mass important later. We numerically investigate the method on the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) equation with a linear source term, Fisher--KPP equations, and Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao gradient flows.
item.dc:creator: Jianguo Hou, Wuchen Li

item.title: A graph discretization of the Steklov and Neumann problems on domains in complete Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.17491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish quantitative spectral convergence for graph discretizations of the Steklov and Neumann problems for bounded domains in complete Riemannian manifolds. Our construction uses weighted proximity graphs built from maximal $\epsilon$-separated sets, with a correction to the discrete energy accounting for the geometry near the boundary. We consider two discrete Steklov problems: one defined using an averaged boundary trace, and the other using restriction to boundary vertices. Both approximate the continuum Steklov spectrum, but under different conditions on the discretization parameters. The additional scale condition required for the restriction-based problem is also necessary for spectral convergence. As a byproduct, we obtain quantitative convergence of the Neumann spectrum. The estimates are uniform under suitable geometric bounds.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Audet-Beaumont

item.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Dynamical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.17503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a multifidelity (MF) formulation of Operator Inference (OpInf) for learning non-intrusive, physics-based reduced-order models (ROMs) of nonlinear dynamical systems. OpInf learns reduced operators from projections of snapshot data by solving a least squares regression problem. However, generating high-fidelity snapshots can be computationally expensive, limiting parameter coverage and the temporal extent of training trajectories for many aerospace applications, which can lead to inaccurate or unstable ROM predictions. This work proposes MF-OpInf, which combines limited high-fidelity snapshots with more plentiful low-fidelity snapshots through a control-variates-inspired MF least squares formulation to learn a single set of reduced operators across multiple trajectories. Low-fidelity trajectories provide additional parameter coverage and extend beyond the high-fidelity training time horizon. The low-fidelity snapshots are also used to construct an improved reduced basis through weighted proper orthogonal decomposition. We demonstrate MF-OpInf on a nonlinear reaction-diffusion problem with parametrized sinusoidal forcing and a two-dimensional incompressible flow past a cylinder with a parametrized inlet pulse. In these experiments, under an equal training simulation budget, MF-OpInf reduces the mean relative prediction error at unseen parameters by up to $87\%$ for the reaction-diffusion problem and $28\%$ for the cylinder flow problem over the test time regime, which extends beyond the high-fidelity training time horizon. These results demonstrate that MF-OpInf can improve temporal extrapolation and prediction at unseen parameters without increasing the training simulation budget.
item.dc:creator: Vignesh Sella, Anirban Chaudhuri, Karen Willcox

item.title: Proximal Adam algorithm for nonsmooth composite optimization and linear convergence under proximal PL geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.17727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze Adam-type methods for nonsmooth composite optimization problems $\min_x\Phi(x)=f(x)+h(x)$, where $f$ is smooth and $h$ is convex, proper, and lower semicontinuous. The nonsmooth term is treated by a metric-weighted proximal map, while the smooth term is preconditioned by the Adam second-moment matrix. We prove a composite descent lemma whose constants depend explicitly on the spectral bounds of the adaptive metric and a residual--step equivalence that converts proximal step decay into subgradient stationarity. These yield an $O(1/N)$ bound on the minimum proximal stationarity residual for the deterministic proximal normalized gradient method without convexity of $f$, and the same $O(1/N)$ rate for proximal Adam under quantitative momentum-alignment and residual-coherence conditions together with a metric-compatibility condition. By estimating the momentum error directly, the same $O(1/N)$ rate is also obtained without the momentum-alignment and residual-coherence assumptions. When the composite objective satisfies a proximal Polyak--{\L}ojasiewicz inequality, both algorithms and the relaxed proximal Adam scheme converge linearly with explicit contraction factors. Numerical experiments on a diagonal Lasso problem, two-dimensional image TV denoising, and two-dimensional elastic parameter identification illustrate the predicted stationarity and linear rates.
item.dc:creator: Xiaopeng Zhu, Zhongyi Huang

item.title: High-probability convergence of adaptive, proximal, and clipped Adam-type methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.17736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper develops a unified high-probability analysis of adaptive, proximal, and clipped first-order methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization. For a smooth objective whose stochastic gradient error has sub-Gaussian norm, the normalized adaptive gradient method attains the standard stochastic nonconvex complexity of the square root of the number of iterations, with an additional logarithmic dependence on the inverse confidence level that is inversely proportional to the number of iterations. The proof uses an adaptive descent decomposition together with Freedman and Bernstein concentration inequalities. The same guarantee is established for the full adaptive moment method under an explicit momentum-alignment condition. The analysis is extended to projected and proximal updates through a stationarity measure based on the subdifferential distance, to objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, and to heavy-tailed noise through truncation. The framework is applied to stochastic inverse problems in elasticity, and numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical scaling and the practical behavior of the methods.
item.dc:creator: Xiaopeng Zhu, Zhongyi Huang

item.title: Scalar Entropic Damage Transport: Well-posed softening with a single damage variable
item.description: arXiv:2611.17822v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Entropic Damage Transport (EDT) represents material softening via a local continuum damage model while ensuring the well-posedness of the mechanical boundary value problem. It is based on a convexification of the time-incremental potential associated with a rate-limited scalar damage model. A one-dimensional distribution of damage states serves as the internal variable, and the number of these states grows with the number of time steps. We show that the emergence of the damage distribution is an artifact of the time discretization. Surprisingly, the distribution concentrates at a single damage state in the time-continuous limit, and EDT converges to a rate-limited damage model with a scalar damage variable, whose free energy is jointly convex in the strain and the reciprocal degradation. We exploit this hidden convexity by a frozen-metric discretization in terms of the reciprocal degradation, which renders every increment jointly convex. The resulting scalar update preserves damage irreversibility, the prescribed damage-rate limitation and thermomechanical consistency, reduces to a scalar equation and provides a symmetric and positive definite algorithmic tangent in closed form. Computational experiments assess the accuracy and the efficiency of both formulations from the material point to the microstructure level, and demonstrate that the scalar update permits a finite-element computation of industrial size with more than 14 million degrees of freedom.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Nutz, Vikram Laheri, Matti Schneider

item.title: Certificate-Based Verification of Pulsed Field Ablation Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.18148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational models of pulsed field ablation predict the lesion as the tissue where the electric field exceeds a lethal threshold. Their numerical error is rarely bounded, and automated pipelines increasingly run them without an expert checking each result. To verify each run, we separate the question "was the stated model solved correctly?" from the solver that answers it. An untrusted solver returns with its answer a certificate, consisting of a potential with the correct electrode and ground values and an exactly charge-conserving current. A small independent checker verifies the certificate against a written specification of the physics. Using the Prager-Synge hypercircle theorem evaluated in ball arithmetic, it turns the certificate into guaranteed two-sided bounds on the impedance and on the root-mean-square field of every tile of a lesion map, also over a range of blood/tissue conductivity ratios. A vectorized version of the checker takes about a tenth of the solve time. For a focal electrode in contact, the tile-resolved depth at 1000 V and 700 V/cm is proven to lie in 3.50-3.75 mm for every ratio from 1.7 to 3.75. For a bipolar catheter, certified depths overlap published in-vivo depths. Where they differ from a published reference model, the certificates prove that the difference is not numerical error in our computation. We compare the certificate with a grid convergence study on the same solver. On graded grids the study is sharper for local fields but remains an estimate. On uniform grids it fails to converge at the electrode edge, where the certificate still gives a valid bracket. Solvers that deliberately solve equations other than the specified ones pass the grid convergence study, but the certificates refute their claims or leave them unsupported.
item.dc:creator: Konstantinos Dovelos

item.title: Balancing-based model reduction for output-constrained optimal control of switched linear systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.18424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a balanced-truncation (BT) framework for model-order reduction of optimal control problems governed by switched linear systems, with quadratic tracking costs, convex input constraints, and Moreau--Yosida-regularized output constraints. For general Petrov--Galerkin reduced models, we derive an a posteriori bound for the error in the optimal value function, and combine it with BT-based estimates of the dynamical-system reduction error. We show that BT preserves the duality structure underlying the first-order optimality conditions, making first-reduce-then-optimize and first-optimize-then-reduce equivalent. Consequently, reducing the forward system also reduces the associated optimality system, leading to a certified, online-efficient, and online-adaptive approximation of the parameterized solution operator. The reduced model can therefore be reused across different regularization parameters, constraint sets, switching signals, and reference trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Michael Kartmann, Mattia Manucci, Benjamin Unger, Stefan Volkwein

item.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
item.description: arXiv:2611.18448v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems. In addition, for a class of single-site Glauber dynamics, we establish error bounds for sparse-plus-low-rank compression and uniform-in-time bounds for connected-cluster approximation and observable propagation with compressed transition moment matrices.
item.dc:creator: Yuehaw Khoo, Bowen Li, Yuguan Wang, Siyao Yang

item.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
item.description: arXiv:2611.18511v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.
item.dc:creator: Brandon Amos

item.title: From smoothed analysis to backward error: The power of adaptive perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2611.18545v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Smoothed analysis has become a central tool in theoretical computer science, often allowing for significant improvements to worst-case running times if we settle for a solution to a small random perturbation of the problem instance. This is closely related to the classical concept of backward error in numerical analysis, which allows an algorithm to return a solution to an arbitrary perturbation of the problem. Despite the qualitative similarity of these concepts, we show that they can exhibit large quantitative differences. Notably, we prove that, while a linear system with any $n \times n$ matrix $A$ can be solved to backward error $\epsilon$ using $O(\log(n) / \epsilon)$ matrix-vector products with $A$, any algorithm that solves a random $\epsilon$-sized perturbation of $A$ requires $\Omega(n)$ matrix-vector products. This means that a useful perturbation for solving a linear system in backward error must be adaptive to the input. Interestingly, however, randomness is still essential: we show that any deterministic method that attains small backward error for all linear systems provably requires $\Omega(n)$ matrix-vector products, resulting in the first separation between randomized and deterministic algorithms in a natural computational model for solving linear systems. Finally, we show that matrix structure can significantly affect backward error complexity. For example, we show a deterministic $O(1/\epsilon)$ matrix-vector product algorithm for symmetric linear systems.
item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Derezi\'nski, Michael W. Mahoney, Raphael A. Meyer, Christopher Musco

item.title: Time Relaxation with Iterative Modified Lavrentiev Regularization
item.description:

From this we obtain sharp consistency bounds, the existence of weak solutions with an energy inequality, and an explicit estimate showing that the energy in scales below any given length is $O(\delta/\chi)$ as $\chi	o\infty$. item.dc:creator: Ming Zhong

item.title: Fully implicit timestepping methods for the rotating shallow water equations
item.description: arXiv:2508.02358v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fully implicit timestepping methods have had limited application in geophysical fluid dynamics due to challenges of finding suitable iterative solvers, since the coupled treatment of advection prevents the standard elimination techniques. However, overlapping Additive Schwarz methods provide a robust, scalable iterative approach for solving the monolithic coupled system for all fields and Runge-Kutta stages. In this study we investigate this approach applied to the rotating shallow water equations, facilitated by the Irksome package which provides automated code generation for implicit Runge-Kutta methods. We compare various schemes in terms of accuracy and efficiency using an implicit/explicit splitting method, namely the ARK2 scheme of Giraldo et al (2013), as a benchmark. This provides an initial look at whether implicit Runge-Kutta methods can be viable for atmosphere and ocean simulation.
item.dc:creator: Werner Bauer, Colin J. Cotter, Joshua Hope-Collins

item.title: A Superfast Direct Solver for Type-III Inverse Nonuniform Discrete Fourier Transform
item.description: arXiv:2512.03733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Various fields in scientific computing require the use of the nonuniform discrete Fourier transform (NUDFT) and its inversion. In [H. Wilber, E. N. Epperly, and A. H. Barnett, SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 47 (2025), pp. A1702-A1732], the authors proposed a direct inversion method for the type-II NUDFT, which achieves quasi-linear complexity by approximating the type-II NUDFT matrix as a product of a hierarchical semiseparable (HSS) matrix and a DFT matrix. In this article, we propose a novel superfast direct inversion method for type-III NUDFT. The proposed method approximates the type-III NUDFT matrix as a product of a type-II NUDFT matrix and an HSS matrix. This decomposition enables both the forward application and the backward inversion to be accomplished with quasi-linear complexity. The fast inversion can serve as a high-accuracy direct solver or as an efficient preconditioner. Additionally, we provide an error bound for the approximation when the sample points are independent and identically distributed uniform random variables and the frequencies are perturbed continuous integers. Numerical results are presented to verify the relevant theoretical properties and demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Yingzhou Li, Jingyu Liu

item.title: Applications of QR-based Vector-Valued Rational Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2601.23237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Several applications of the QR-AAA algorithm, a greedy scheme for vector-valued rational approximation, are presented. The focus is on demonstrating the flexibility and practical effectiveness of QR-AAA in a variety of computational settings, including Stokes flow computation, multivariate rational approximation, function extension, the development of novel quadrature methods and near-field approximation in the boundary element method.
item.dc:creator: Simon Dirckx, Joar Bagge, Daan Huybrechs

item.title: Explicit Planar Finite Element Elasticity Complexes and $C^1$ Elements on Barycentric Refinements
item.description: arXiv:2604.26701v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a closed-form realization of the finite element elasticity complex associated with the Arnold--Douglas--Gupta family on barycentric refinements. Their construction implies the existence of minimal $C^1$ potential spaces, but does not provide explicit general-degree scalar enrichments. On each macrotriangle, we derive three divergence-free stress enrichments and their Airy potentials. For every degree $q\geq4$, the resulting potential space enriches $\mathbb P_q$ by three explicit functions. A geometric decomposition yields unisolvent degrees of freedom and $C^1$ assembly without vertex supersmoothness. The space attains the dimension bound for macroelements containing $\mathbb P_q$ with full polynomial boundary trace freedom. Its Airy image is the divergence-free subspace of the corresponding stress space, and global assembly gives an exact discrete elasticity complex on simply connected domains. The low-order spaces $U_2$ and $U_3$ recover the reduced and full Hsieh--Clough--Tocher spaces, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Chunyu Chen, Long Chen, Xuehai Huang

item.title: Finding accurate eigenvalues and eigenvectors of positive semi-definite matrices given a subspace
item.description: arXiv:2605.05043v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit a classical problem in numerical linear algebra: given a $k$-dimensional subspace $\mathcal{Q}$ with orthonormal basis $Q$ that approximates the leading eigenspace of an $n\times n$ positive semi-definite matrix $A$, the goal is to extract high-accuracy eigenvalues. The Rayleigh-Ritz (RR) method is the standard algorithm for the task, which has been shown to be optimal in several ways (when $A$ is symmetric, not necessarily positive semi-definite $A\succeq 0$). In this paper, we show that when $A\succeq 0$, alternative methods can outperform RR, including Nystr{\"o}m and one-sided projected SVD, while having the same computational complexity; that is, the main cost is in computing $AQ$, plus an $O(nk^2)$ term. In particular, we advocate the use of Nystr{\"o}m's method, quantitatively showing that the approximate leading eigenvalues have better accuracy than RR, and the improvement can be arbitrarily large. The significant accuracy improvement occurs for the first $i$ eigenvalues if $\lambda_i \gg \lambda_{k+1}$ and uniformly for all $k$ eigenvalues if $\lambda_k \gg \lambda_{k+1}$. This theoretical observation can be extended to the case where we extract $k$ leading eigenvalues from a larger-dimensional subspace. A similar improvement is numerically observed for the purpose of approximating the leading eigenvectors. In contrast, when the target eigenvalues are the trailing ones, the situation is reversed, and the Nystr{\"o}m method performs poorly; we suggest a remedy based on a shift for this situation.
item.dc:creator: Yuji Nakatsukasa, Zheng Tang

item.title: A constrained Onsager variational framework for parametric approximations of Willmore and Helfrich flows
item.description: arXiv:2608.07244v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a constrained Onsager variational framework for parametric finite element approximations of Willmore and Helfrich flows. The weak curvature relation is used as a PDE constraint to express the first variation of the bending energy in curvature-vector form. Onsager's principle then combines this variation with dissipation based on the normal velocity, while an independent relaxed minimal-deformation-rate (relaxed-MDR) constraint selects the tangential velocity. The resulting mixed formulation admits a semidiscretization by continuous piecewise linear elements that satisfies an exact energy-dissipation law and exactly preserves area and volume when the corresponding constraints are imposed. The framework accommodates constant spontaneous curvature and applies to both closed surfaces and open surfaces with fixed boundaries under Navier or clamped conditions. We also propose a linearly implicit fully discrete scheme, prove its unique solvability, and present numerical experiments demonstrating convergence, energy decay, constraint preservation, and effective mesh redistribution.
item.dc:creator: Quan Zhao

item.title: The least-squares RBF-PU method for linear elasticity in the diaphragm geometry
item.description: arXiv:2608.23718v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The human diaphragm is vital for respiration and its simulation can aid in further understanding complications arising in individuals that have been subjected to mechanical ventilation. The diaphragm is very thin and hence its numerical simulation poses a challenge for most numerical methods. In this paper, we compute the deformation of real diaphragm geometries, which are modelled as linearly elastic, and are subject to realistic boundary conditions. The method used is the unfitted least-squares radial basis function partition of unity method. The patches used are cylindrical and refinement is performed along the thin direction of the diaphragm. Both the unfitted nature of the method as well as the refinement technique make this method particularly well suited to solve problems formulated in thin geometries. We derive a theoretical proof showing that the method converges with high order to the solution of a well-posed linear elasticity boundary value problem.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Michael, Elisabeth Larsson, Pierre-Fr\'ed\'eric Villard, Davoud Mirzaei

item.title: Mean Square Error Analysis of Stochastic Runge-Kutta Integrators
item.description: arXiv:2609.11528v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze the mean square error of stochastic Runge--Kutta integrators for overdamped Langevin dynamics whose potential is strongly convex outside a bounded region. A decomposition splits the local error into a mean-zero term and a smaller remainder, and the discrete Poisson equation turns their moments into a bound on the error of a time average. We carry this out for two stochastic Runge--Kutta integrators proposed by Yang \& Wang (2026), both of strong order $\frac32$ and weak order $2$, which evaluate the gradient of the potential and no higher derivative. We show that their laws approach the law of the exact solution at second order in Wasserstein-1 distance, up to a logarithm, uniformly in the number of steps. For a test function with bounded derivatives up to third order, we prove that the mean square error over $N$ steps with step size $h$ is $\mathcal O ( \frac{1}{Nh} + h^4 )$, which is the optimal order in the discretization. Experiments measure the strong and weak orders and the sampling bias on a nonconvex potential in $\mathbb R^2$, and compare the integrators on a diffusion model of CIFAR-10.
item.dc:creator: Xuda Ye

item.title: Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
item.description: arXiv:2610.22063v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Past work with Tom Seidman analyzed the spatial convergence order of the numerical finite element method applied to time-dependent diffusion-reaction equations with a measure-valued source term. For smooth source terms, the numerical method has second-order accuracy, but the non-smooth source terms introduce a limitation of the order that depends on the spatial dimension. This work in honor of Tom extends the analysis to the finite volume method in its clas- sical two-point flux form and shows that the regularity of the source term reduces the convergence order to 1 in two and 0.5 in three spatial dimensions which is reduced from the nominal second-order and depends on the space dimension. Computational tests with a point source modeled by a Dirac delta distribution exhibit the behavior predicted by the analytical results.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Gobbert, Martin Kru\v{z}\'ik, Andreas Meister, Michael Muscedere

item.title: Triple Products of Correlated Multivariate Hermite Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.30204v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stochastic Galerkin schemes (SGS) are used to approximate solutions to differential equations with stochastic parameters. In particular, they express the solution with an infinite orthogonal functional basis of the parameter space and derive a deterministic surrogate system of PDEs whose solution approximates that of the original stochastic problem. When the parameters are correlated, the infinite series representation of the solution does not provably converge for all joint distributions; further, classic decorrelating transformations (e.g., Rosenblatt, Nataf) often introduce known numerical instabilities. Rahman (2017) established convergence in probability and distribution for correlated Gaussian parameters when the basis functionals are multivariate Hermite polynomials (MHPs), where these polynomials are only weakly orthogonal with respect to the underlying joint density. Due to weak orthogonality, the $N$th moments of MHPs that emerge during Galerkin projection do not trivially decompose into products of one-dimensional expectations via tensorization. Namely, an $N$th-order moment has no closed-form expression for $N > 2$ and consequently is estimated numerically. Because the number of such moments grows combinatorially with parameter dimension and polynomial degree, approximating each one individually via sampling or quadrature can quickly become cost-prohibitive. In this paper, we introduce and prove several foundational properties of MHPs. These results culminate in an explicit formula for evaluating the $N = 3$ moments (triple products) directly without numerical estimation.
item.dc:creator: Laura Lyman

item.title: A Second-Order Stochastic Dynamic Mode Decomposition by Richardson Extrapolation
item.description: arXiv:2611.00793v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stochastic dynamic mode decomposition (SDMD) approximates the Koopman semigroup of an It\^o diffusion by a Galerkin generator matrix on a dictionary of observables, computed from samples of the invariant law and generator evaluations, and advances observables with a first-order stochastic Taylor step (SDMD-1). The second-order Taylor step (SDMD-2) also needs a third matrix, a dictionary with four derivatives, and a fourth-order differential operator evaluated at every sample. Richardson extrapolation of the SDMD-1 step (SDMD-R) is second-order accurate with the data, the matrices, and the regularity of SDMD-1. The error bound, for exact and empirical matrices, consists of the Galerkin error of the dictionary, a time-stepping term, and a data term of order $m^{-1/2}$ in the sample size $m$. Relative to the Galerkin semigroup, the limit of the schemes as the time step $\dt\to0$, the time-stepping error is $O(\dt^2)$ for SDMD-R and $O(\Theta_N\dt+\dt^2)$ for SDMD-2, with $\Theta_N$ the norm of the second-order Galerkin residual $\Proj_N\cA(I-\Proj_N)\cA|_{\cV_N}$, and the first-order term is attained. For reversible periodic diffusions and trigonometric dictionaries with cutoff $K$, the step restriction $\dt\lesssim K^{-2}$ makes all three schemes contractions, and the error against the Koopman semigroup on $H^\ell$ observables is $O(K^{-(\ell-2)}+\dt^p)$ plus a data term of order $K^{d+2}(m^{-1}\log K)^{1/2}$ in dimension $d$, with $p=1$ for SDMD-1 and $p=2$ for SDMD-R and SDMD-2. In experiments with trigonometric dictionaries the errors of SDMD-R and SDMD-2 differ by at most ten percent. For a spline dictionary with two derivatives, SDMD-R remains second-order accurate, whereas SDMD-2 with pointwise evaluations is first-order accurate.
item.dc:creator: Yuanchao Xu

item.title: Improving Matrix Exponential for Generative AI Flows: A Taylor-Based Approach Beyond Paterson--Stockmeyer
item.description: arXiv:2512.20777v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The matrix exponential is a fundamental operator in scientific computing and system simulation, with applications ranging from control theory and quantum mechanics to modern generative machine learning. While Pad\'e approximants combined with scaling and squaring have long served as the standard, recent Taylor-based methods, which utilize polynomial evaluation schemes that surpass the classical Paterson--Stockmeyer technique, offer superior accuracy and reduced computational complexity. This paper presents an optimized Taylor-based algorithm for the matrix exponential, specifically designed for the high-throughput requirements of generative AI flows. We provide a rigorous error analysis and develop a dynamic selection strategy for the Taylor order and scaling factor to minimize computational effort under a prescribed error tolerance. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate that our approach provides significant acceleration and maintains high numerical stability compared to existing state-of-the-art implementations. These results establish the proposed method as a highly efficient tool for large-scale generative modeling.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Sastre, Daniel Faronbi, Jos\'e Miguel Alonso, Peter Traver, Javier Ib\'a\~nez, Nuria Lloret

item.title: Kernel-based potential mean-field games with unbiased random Fourier $U$-statistics
item.description: arXiv:2605.29371v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the subclass of potential mean-field games in which the running interaction cost and the terminal target cost are both expressed through reproducing-kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) penalties, and develop a computational framework that exploits this kernel structure. Both costs are estimated from finite-sample empirical distributions using a random Fourier U-statistic representation that is unbiased and has linear cost in the batch size. The drift of the controlled diffusion is parametrized by a neural network and trained via stochastic gradient descent. For population near-minimizers we prove convergence to the terminal-constrained problem as the penalty diverges, and show that the same limit is recovered almost surely when such controls are evaluated on independent finite samples under explicit coupling conditions on the penalty, random-feature count and sample size. The framework includes the kernel-MMD-penalty Schr{\"o}dinger bridge problem as the special case of a vanishing interaction cost. Numerical experiments illustrate the method on the Schr{\"o}dinger bridge problem in dimensions up to one hundred, and on an electric vehicle charging coordination problem with per-vehicle physical heterogeneity, where a control-dependent aggregate-demand cost produces a trade-off between peak normalized charging power and the terminal service level.
item.dc:creator: Yumiharu Nakano

item.title: A Spectral Proximal DC Algorithm with Nonmonotone Line Search and Extrapolation
item.description: arXiv:2608.03465v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The paper proposes a novel proximal difference-of-convex (DC) algorithmic framework to solve general nonconvex, nonsmooth optimization problems. The basic pBBDCA method combines Barzilai-Borwein (BB) parameter selection with a nonmonotone directional line search, requiring only one proximal solve per iteration. We also develop two extrapolated variants using restart and safeguarding mechanisms. The global convergence of the proposed framework is rigorously established under the Kurdyka-\L ojasiewicz property. Numerical experiments on the SCAD-regularized least squares problem and graph Ginzburg-Landau image segmentation models demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve highly competitive efficiency and accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Kelin Wu, Hongpeng Sun

item.title: Kusner's conjecture on equilateral sets is false
item.description: arXiv:2608.14013v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We disprove Kusner's 1983 conjecture that every equilateral set in $\ell_p^n$ with $2<p<\infty$ has at most $n+1$ points: there exist $58$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{56}$ whose pairwise $\ell_5$ distances are all equal, so the maximum equilateral-set size satisfies $e(\ell_5^{56})\ge58>57$. This is the first equilateral set of more than $n+1$ points in $\ell_p^n$ for any finite $p\ge2$. The construction persists on an open interval of exponents around $5$. The configuration is specified by the unique solution of an explicit polynomial system with rational coefficients in a rational box; existence and uniqueness are proved by exact integer inequalities. The existence of the $58$-point equilateral set in $\ell_5^{56}$ has been formalised in Lean from standard axioms.
item.dc:creator: Logan R. Chalmers

item.title: The $\alpha$-Limit Problem: Convergence of a Linear Degenerate Interface Transmission Problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.01237v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the singular limit of a family of linear degenerate interface transmission problems arising from a regularization procedure in the newly proposed Two-Parameter Diffuse Domain Method (DDM2p). For $\alpha>0$, the regularized problem admits a strictly convex variational formulation on $H^{1}(\Omega)$. In the limit $\alpha\to0$, the problem degenerates to a weakly coupled interface system with a nonstandard energy structure. To characterize the limit, we introduce a closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal{H}\subset H^{1}(\Omega)$, defined through an auxiliary Helmholtz problem on an annular subdomain $\Omega_2\subset \Omega$, and identify the limiting energy functional $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ on $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that the regularized energies $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha}$ restricted to $\mathcal{H}$ $\Gamma$-converge to $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ in the strong $L^{2}(\Omega)$ topology, using the standard framework. Consequently, minimizers of $\mathcal{E}_{\alpha}$ converge to the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{E}_{0}$, which is shown to be equivalent to the solution of the limiting interface problem. We further prove a strong convergence $u_{\alpha}\to u_{0}$ in $H^{1}(\Omega)$ and establish a convergence rate of $O(\alpha)$. Numerical experiments in one spatial dimension exhibit first-order convergence, suggesting that the proved $O(\alpha)$ upper bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Toai Luong, Tadele Mengesha, Kerrek Stinson, Steven M. Wise, Ming Hei Wong

item.title: Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.12654v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic operator equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper formalizes the reduction process and proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a fast one-time symbolic phase via its sparse prefix-sum property, the runtime bus-type projection overhead and indirect mapping caches are entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The proposed algorithm is implemented in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 28.1-37.9 times faster than the MATPOWER-style baseline and 8.9-9.7 times faster than the in-house Sch\"afer-Braun-inspired assembly (V1); on PEGASE 9241, it outperforms optimized traditional C++ assembly routines by 3.72 times in cold construction and 2.59 times across iterations. End-to-end, the iteration-loop solve time with KLU is 1.16-1.97 times faster than the native C++ LightSim2Grid and up to 95.5 times faster than pandapower, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.
item.dc:creator: Tianshi Cheng, Venkata Dinavahi
